newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent sheds gains after NYMEX crude falls.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent sheds gains after NYMEX crude falls.

text.p: IPE Brent futures shed all of its earlier gains to trade lower after NYMEX slipped, traders said.
June Brent was trading six cents down at $18.63 a barrel by 1501 GMT after NYMEX fell to as low as $20.18.
Gas oil was also trading at a lower level, only 50 cents up at $169.50 after trading as high as $2.00 up earlier in the day.
"It (Brent) just came off more than 20 points and no one knows why. NYMEX fell but we don't know why. We haven't heard any news," one broker said.
Earlier a trader said that he was cautious of the gains made by crude since Thursday, when June Brent closed a hefty 55 cents up at $18.69.
"I question the crude's move on the upside," the broker said.

"I am very cautious, it has not been confirmed by the gasoline...I need to see (NYMEX) gasoline confirmation, minimum a break above 62.90 (cents a gallon), probably confirmed by a break above 63.40 (cents a gallon), which is the high we made last week," the broker said.
Unleaded gasoline futures for May were trading at 62.80 cents a gallon, or 0.30 cent higher, by 1511 GMT.
Another broker said that Brent's rally on Thursday was mostly from talks of operational problems in the gasoline production units at two U.S. Gulf refineries.
"The question is whether we see it supporting the market today," he added. The two U.S. companies have declined to comment on the speculation.
